body.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{face}}\), the recovery map is well-defined and \(\Phi(p)=\theta\). More strongly, for every \(\widetilde P\in\mathcal F(p)\), the formulas recover the same \(\pi_j^d\), the same component law of \((Z,X_0,X_1,X_2,X_3)\) in each cohort, and the same \(\tau_j\) and \(\tau\), up to the declared descending \(\rho_j^d\) order. The result holds without time homogeneity and on laws with the common absorbing row that violate the all-state terminal-rank and positive-transition conditions used by the adjacent recovery theorems.
body.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: it converts four observable active minors and stochastic normalization into latent path and ATT recovery on a structurally singular support face.
body.gap: Ahn and Kasahara, Proposition 14 and Appendix A.4, and Higgins and Jochmans, Theorem 1, recover latent Markov laws through full-rank spectral factorizations, but their stated conditions do not cover a state that is absorbing for every type; the present claim proves fiberwise recovery on that excluded face.
body.consumer: Rao and Risch's incumbent-firm panel can use low- and high-productivity active states plus exit to distinguish offsetting type-specific exit responses hidden by a nearly flat aggregate exit effect.
